Figure_R0_sphere.description: Adapted from Jas et al. (2026), CC BY 4.0 (bioRxiv 2026.08.17.744953; the preprint's Fig. 4E, redrawn from our reimplementation of its spherical model). (a) Sphere of the preprint: head radius 95 mm, brain radius 80 mm, 30-nAm tangential dipole, OPM on the scalp (standoff 0 mm), SQUID 18 mm above it, single-channel SNR = peak radial field / noise. SNR_OPM = SNR_SQUID where B_OPM / B_SQUID = eta, so the curve is the depth at which the stored field ratio of results/g1a/g1a_curves.csv equals eta (log-linear interpolation between its 100 grid depths, 15-94.2 mm), from the sphere centre (eta0 = 1.6829, depth 95 mm) to the brain surface (eta1 = 5.3086, depth 15 mm); dots: the stored exact roots of Eq. 3 at eta 1.7, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5 (curve within 0.0053 mm of them). Shaded: depths where the OPM's SNR is higher (every depth for eta < eta0); dotted line: the brain surface. Open diamond: the equal-SNR depth the preprint prints for eta = 3 (28 mm, with its Fig. 3; drawn there at 27.53 mm; exact root 27.67 mm). (b) Realistic adult head (MNE sample subject, 3-layer BEM, 10-nAm cortical-normal dipoles), the G2 bridge: per target the peak |B| of the OPM array over that of the best Neuromag magnetometer; medians over targets in 5-mm bins of depth below the scalp (distance to the nearest MRI scalp point); d_eq(eta) = the depth where that median falls below eta, linearly interpolated between bin centres (sensor white noise only, peak-channel SNR, magnetometers as the comparator, as in the sphere); eta grid 1-6 in steps of 0.25. Points are drawn where a crossing exists: site-matched OPM array eta 2.5-4.75: 13.4-41.9 mm; dense OPM array eta 2.5-5.25: 13.3-45.1 mm; the OPM leads in every depth bin for eta 1-2.25 (both arrays) and Neuromag already in the shallowest bin for eta >= 5 (site-matched) and >= 5.5 (dense). Dashed: the sphere of (a) with the real median standoffs (OPM site-matched array 6.99 mm, Neuromag magnetometer coils 29.83 mm from the scalp). Depth axis inverted (deeper down) and shared by both panels.
Figure_R0_sphere.alt: Two line charts of the equal-SNR depth below the scalp (vertical axis inverted, deeper down) against the noise ratio eta from 1 to 6. Left, the sphere: the depth falls from the sphere centre at eta 1.68 to the brain surface at eta 5.31; above the curve the OPM's SNR is higher; an open diamond marks the preprint's printed 28 mm at eta 3, next to the exact 27.7 mm. Right, the realistic adult head: the site-matched and dense OPM arrays cross between 13 and 45 mm for eta 2.5 to 5.25, close to the dashed sphere with the real standoffs.
Figure_R0_sphere.caption_draft: The spherical benchmark and the realistic head. (a) Depth below the scalp at which an OPM on the scalp and a SQUID 18 mm above it have equal single-channel SNR, against their noise ratio eta, in the adult sphere of Jas et al. (2026) (head radius 95 mm, brain radius 80 mm, 30-nAm tangential dipole; our reimplementation; dots: exact roots; shaded: OPM SNR higher). A crossing exists only for eta between 1.68 and 5.31; the diamond marks the 28 mm printed in the preprint at eta = 3 (exact 27.7 mm). (b) The same quantity on the realistic adult head: depth at which the median over targets of the peak field of the OPM array over that of the best Neuromag magnetometer equals eta (sensor noise only), for the site-matched (98 sites) and dense (208 sites) arrays, and the sphere of (a) with the real median standoffs (7.0 and 29.8 mm). Adapted from Jas et al. (2026), CC BY 4.0.

Figure_R11_maps_adult.description: D = 20 log10(detect_<array>_opm / detect_squid_combined) per cortical target of the adult G2 run (MNE sample subject at its measured head position, 7,661 targets, 10-nAm cortical-normal dipoles, sensor white noise + cortical background, oracle covariance), drawn at the target's vertex of the oct-6 source space on the inflated white surface. The median over all targets is 1.168 dB (dense) and 0.077 dB (site-matched), equal to the stored median log2 ratios times 20 log10 2 (1.168 and 0.077 dB; checked). Under the pediatric convention (area-weighted median, medial wall excluded) the dense array's D at the same pose is 1.274 dB (results/g3b/g3b_summary.json placement_D['adult/centred/combined/intrinsic+brain']; that run's per-target D at this pose agrees with G2's within 0.0092 dB). Light grey: medial wall (targets in FreeSurfer's 'unknown' region: the cut through the corpus callosum and midbrain, not cortex); dark grey: source-space vertices that are not targets, i.e. within 4 mm of the 5,120-triangle inner-skull mesh or outside it (A-BEM-DIST; the shallowest cortex, which the noise model also leaves out of the brain background). A triangle takes the category of at least two of its vertices. Diverging colour scale (red: OPM higher), -6 to +6 dB, shared by R11, R13 and R14 (display choice); values beyond it take the end colour (colour bar extension: 'max'). Views: orthographic, left lateral, left medial, right medial, right lateral, with sulcal shading (opmsquid.plotting); each hemisphere fills its panel (not to scale). Medial wall: 558 targets; not targets: 535 of 8,196 source-space vertices.
Figure_R11_maps_adult.alt: Inflated left and right cortical hemispheres in lateral and medial views, two rows. Top, the dense OPM array against Neuromag's 306 channels: red almost everywhere (99.9% of targets above 0 dB), strongest on lateral convexities, paler on medial and ventral surfaces. Bottom, the site-matched array: a mix of pale red and blue (55% above 0 dB), blue on the ventral and polar temporal and frontal surfaces. Grey: medial wall (light) and scattered vertices near the inner skull (dark).
Figure_R11_maps_adult.caption_draft: D on the adult's inflated cortex (MNE sample subject at its measured head position; sensor plus brain noise; 10-nAm dipoles), lettered (c) in the image (the report shows it below Figure R1's panels): the dense array (208 sites, top) and the site-matched array (98 sites, bottom) against Neuromag's 306 channels; red: the OPM's detectability is higher. Median D +1.17 dB (dense) and +0.08 dB (site-matched) over all 7,661 targets (dense array, area-weighted without the medial wall: +1.27 dB). Light grey: medial wall; dark grey: cortex within 4 mm of the inner skull, which is not simulated as a target and is also left out of the brain background. The colour scale is that of Figure R13.

Figure_R12_geometry.description: Head-frame sections (Neuromag convention of each head's own fiducials; x right, y anterior, z up; mm) through the head origin: sagittal x = 0 and coronal y = 0. Lines: the intersection of the MRI scalp mesh (black) and, in the coronal sections, of the white-matter surfaces (grey; the cortical sources lie on them) with the plane, one segment per crossed triangle (the midsagittal plane passes between the hemispheres, so the sagittal sections show the scalp only), as polylines rounded to 0.01 mm; the sections are cropped below z = -68 mm (face and neck). Markers: sensors within 20 mm of the plane, projected onto it (the slab of results/g3b/Figure_G3B_geometry.png). Filled black squares: the 102 Neuromag magnetometer coil centres of the fixed adult helmet (VectorView geometry of the sample recording) with the head at top contact (the adult's measured pose, then raised along device +z until the nearest coil is 20 mm from the scalp; moved adult 5.5 mm, 12-month template 33.5 mm, child B 26.5 mm). Open vermillion squares: the helmet fitted at the adult's gap (the constant-gap control of results/g3b_constant_gap/g3b_constant_gap_summary.json): the Neuromag helmet scaled by k about the head origin of the laterally centred head (the adult's measured pose shifted along device x to equal left/right median gaps, x shift -1.5 mm, -2.5 mm, -2.5 mm, not raised to top contact) until the median magnetometer-to-scalp gap equals the adult's (29.55 mm, the adult's own helmet laterally centred, k = 1), with no coil centre within the 18-mm Dewar spacing of the scalp or inside the head (where that limit is reached first, k is the smallest feasible factor and the gap is larger: Child C (8.7 y) (not drawn) is clearance-bound at 32.8 mm): k = 1.0000, 0.8552, 0.8769; the coil centres are those exported by scripts/export_g3b_geometry.py, which recomputes this helmet with the constant-gap study's code and reproduces its scale factors and gaps. The helmet scaled with the head (laterally centred; k = 1.0000, 0.8409, 0.8644) is not drawn: its coil centres lie within 2.5 mm of the fitted helmet's in these heads (adult 0.0 mm, 12-month template 2.5 mm, child B 2.2 mm), which the markers could not separate. Open blue circles: the dense OPM sites (sensing centres, 7 mm from the scalp) refitted to each head (208, 144, 153 sites). Order: adult, 12-month template (ANTS12-0Months3T), child B (sub-Z209, OpenNeuro ds005234). Median magnetometer-to-scalp gap (nearest MRI scalp vertex, all 102 coils), stored, and recomputed by the export from the unrounded geometry (equal within 1e-6 mm): fixed helmet at top contact 28.38, 40.42, 38.40 mm; helmet fitted at the adult's gap 29.55, 29.55, 29.55 mm. Sections, coil centres and OPM sites are read from results/g3b/g3b_geometry_sections.json (checked: runs, moves, scale factors, gaps, site counts; the drawn coil centres equal the exported transforms applied to the device-frame coil centres within 0.0050 mm, the effect of the rounding); the coil centres are drawn, not the Dewar surface. Infant template: O'Reilly et al. (2021), built from the Neurodevelopmental MRI Database (Richards et al., 2016); child B: OpenNeuro ds005234 (Fadeev et al., 2024, 2025).
Figure_R12_geometry.alt: Six panels: sagittal (top) and coronal (bottom) sections of three heads, adult, 12-month template and child B, drawn at the same scale. Each shows the scalp outline (the coronal ones with the folded white-matter outline inside), open blue circles of the dense OPM sites hugging the scalp, filled black squares of the fixed adult helmet and open vermillion squares of the helmet fitted at the adult's gap. Around the adult the two helmets nearly coincide; around the two smaller heads the fixed helmet touches at the top and leaves a wide gap at the sides, front and back (median 40 and 38 mm against the adult's 28 mm), while the fitted helmet is shrunk to follow the head at the adult's gap (29.6 mm in each).
Figure_R12_geometry.caption_draft: Helmet geometry, lettered (d) in the image (the report shows it below Figure R15's panels (a) to (c)). Sagittal (top) and coronal (bottom) sections through the head origin of the adult, the 12-month template and child B, at the same scale: scalp (black) and, in the coronal sections, white-matter surface (grey); filled squares, the Neuromag magnetometers of the fixed adult helmet with the head at top contact; open squares, the helmet fitted at the adult's gap (the Neuromag helmet scaled about the laterally centred head until its median magnetometer-to-scalp gap equals the adult's, 29.6 mm; scale factor above each column); circles, the dense OPM sites; only sensors within 20 mm of the section are drawn. Median magnetometer-to-scalp gap in the fixed helmet 28.4, 40.4, 38.4 mm (adult, 12-month template, child B); in the fitted helmet it is the adult's, 29.6 mm, in each head.

Figure_R15_arrays.description: The adult (MNE sample subject) in its head frame (Neuromag convention from the digitised fiducials: x towards the right preauricular point, y towards the nasion, z up; mm), in orthographic projection, seen from the right (top row: view along -x, anterior to the right) and from above (bottom row: view along -z, anterior up), all panels at one scale. Head: the boundary-element head surface of the forward model on the MRI scalp (2562 vertices, 5120 triangles; conformed to the MRI scalp, vertices moved a median 1.05 mm), drawn with smooth grey shading lit from the viewer's side and its visible outline; the side view is cut at z = -70 mm (neck). Markers: a sensor is drawn when no part of the head surface lies between it and the viewer and, in the side view, when it is on the right half of the head (x > 0), so that the far side's sensors do not overlap the near side's (drawn, side/top: Neuromag 47/102; site-matched OPM 44/96; dense OPM 99/206). (a) Neuromag (306 channels): the 102 magnetometer coil centres of the sample recording (each of the sensor sites also holds two planar gradiometers) at the adult's measured head position, the primary position of the adult analyses; median 29.8 mm from the scalp (nearest MRI scalp vertex; 5th-95th percentile 25.4-35.9 mm). (b) Site-matched OPM array: the Neuromag sites that fit the OPM placement rules, each projected onto the scalp (98 of 102; the sites of magnetometers MEG 0111, MEG 0141, MEG 1421, MEG 1431 excluded), at least 22.1 mm apart. (c) Dense OPM array: the densest feasible single-axis array under the packing rule (208 sites, at least 17.0 mm apart). OPM markers are the sensing centres, 7 mm from the scalp along the head-surface normal (median distance to the nearest MRI scalp vertex 6.99 and 7.00 mm); each OPM measures the field component along the head-surface normal. Colours: Okabe-Ito, the report's array colours (Neuromag black, site-matched OPM sky blue, dense OPM blue). The channel-budget control of the adult analyses (204 sites, a subset of the dense array) is not analysed in the main text and not drawn. Positions and head surface are read from results/g2/g2_arrays.json, exported by scripts/export_g2_arrays.py, which rebuilds the adult run's arrays with its code and reproduces every array descriptor and sensor-to-scalp distance stored in results/g2/g2_summary.json (checked again here: site counts, descriptors, distances).
Figure_R15_arrays.alt: Six panels in two rows: a grey, smoothly shaded adult head seen from the right (top row) and from above (bottom row), with three arrays in the three columns. Left: 102 black squares of the Neuromag helmet form a shell that stands off the head by about 3 cm, lower at the back than at the front. Middle: 98 sky-blue squares sit on the scalp in the same pattern, the Neuromag sites pulled in onto the head. Right: 208 blue circles cover the scalp above the brow and ears more densely (208 against 98 sites).
Figure_R15_arrays.caption_draft: Sensor arrays on the adult head (MNE sample subject), seen from the right (top; sensors on the right half of the head) and from above (bottom). (a) Neuromag (306 channels): its 102 sensor sites (magnetometer coil centres; each site also holds two planar gradiometers) at the adult's measured head position, a median 29.8 mm from the scalp. (b) Site-matched OPM array (98 sites): Neuromag's sites that fit the OPM placement rules, projected onto the scalp. (c) Dense OPM array (208 sites, at least 17 mm apart). OPM sensing centres lie 7 mm from the scalp; each OPM measures the field component normal to the head surface. Head: the boundary-element head surface of the forward model.
